questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Disorders: Comorbidity in a Table of Two Diagnoses and an Outcome
questions.learningObjective: Identify the term for co-occurring diagnoses
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief for a screening tool asks why two diagnoses often appear together; which term names that overlap?

options.text: Comorbidity, meaning two or more disorders present in the same person
Comorbidity, meaning a single disorder with two names
options.misconception: confuses co-occurrence with synonymy of labels

options.text: Prevalence, the share of a population carrying one diagnosis
Incidence, the rate of new cases appearing over time

questions.explanation: Comorbidity names co-occurring diagnoses in one person, not population rates or synonyms. The tempting wrong ideas swap it for prevalence or incidence.
questions.hint: Think of two disorders in one person

answer.exemplar: The p factor is a general dimension of psychopathology that captures shared risk across many disorders, suggesting common underlying vulnerability rather than entirely separate diseases.
